The rest of chapter 17F.100: .020 Permit Required, .030 Permit Exemptions (faucet and valve repairs, clearing stoppages), .040 Unapproved Work, .050 Disposal of Liquid Waste, .060 Use of License, .070 Plumbing Inspector, .080 Hearing Officer. fixtures.basis: Chapter 17F.040 (Building Code) has no section on the number of plumbing fixtures, separate facilities or all-gender rooms, and SMC 17F.100.010 adds nothing on fixture counts. The only Spokane text that names the fixture table is SMC 17F.070.260, Sanitation Requirements, in the Existing Building and Conservation Code: it starts 'In addition to IBC subsection 2902.1 and Washington State Amendments Table 2902.1' and adds only rules on fixture materials, water supply and sewer connection for existing buildings; it does not change a count. The state table and rules in WAC 51-50-2902 apply unchanged: business 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 after; restaurants 1 per 75; educational 1 per 35 male, 1 per 25 female; urinals optional (2902.1.1.2); separate rooms not required at 25 or fewer (business) or 30 or fewer (dining).
fixtures.quote: In addition to IBC subsection 2902.1 and Washington State Amendments Table 2902.1: ... all plumbing fixtures must be of glazed earthenware or other similar approved nonabsorbent material ... all sanitary facilities must be installed and maintained in a safe and sanitary condition.
fixtures.quote_note: SMC 17F.070.260, Ordinance C35389 section 13, passed 2016-05-23, effective 2016-06-30.
fixtures.state_quote: Educational facilities | 1 per 35 | 1 per 25 | 1 per 85 | 1 per 50
fixtures.confidence: high that Spokane has no amendment to the counts (the whole chapter's section list was read and none concerns plumbing fixtures)

permit.exempt_list_quote: Exemptions from permit requirements of this code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of this code or any other laws or ordinances of this jurisdiction. Permits shall not be required for the following: Building: One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided that the floor area is not greater than 120 square feet (11 m2). Fences not over 7 feet (2134 mm) high. Oil derricks. Retaining walls that are not over 4 feet (1219 mm) in height measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless supporting a surcharge or impounding Class I, II or IIIA liquids. Water tanks supported directly on grade if the capacity is not greater than 5,000 gallons (18 925 L) and the ratio of height to diameter or width is not greater than 2:1. Sidewalks and driveways not more than 30 inches (762 mm) above adjacent grade, and not over any basement or story below and are not part of an accessible route. Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. Prefabricated swimming pools accessory to a Group R-3 occupancy that are less than 24 inches (610 mm) deep, are not greater than 5,000 gallons (18 925 L) and are installed entirely above ground. Shade cloth structures constructed for nursery or agricultural purposes, not including service systems. Swings and other playground equipment accessory to detached one- and two-family dwellings. Window awnings in Group R-3 and U occupancies, supported by an exterior wall that do not project more than 54 inches (1372 mm) from the exterior wall and do not require additional support. Nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) in height.
permit.source_note: Spokane has no exempt list of its own. Its former list (SMC 17F.040.070, 'Permits', which rewrote Sections 105.1 and 105.2) was repealed: 'Repealed by ORD C35389', passed 2016-05-23, effective 2016-06-30. What applies is Section 105.2 of the International Building Code as Washington adopts it, quoted here from UpCodes' copy of the Washington State Building Code 2021 (a secondary copy: ICC's site blocks scripts). SMC 17G.010.010 adds one sentence: 'Exemption from a permit requirement is not exemption from the other requirements of this code.'

restrooms_city.note: No Spokane ordinance or building code amendment on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms was found: chapter 17F.040 has no section on toilet rooms or signs, and one web search for a Spokane restroom ordinance returned only Seattle's and Tacoma's and news reports of a 2025 Spokane anti-discrimination ordinance (not read; no restroom signage rule reported). The state building code applies: single-user rooms 'shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex' (2021 International Building Code Section 2902.1.2, unamended by Washington; read in Seattle's official print of the 2021 code, where it carries no state or Seattle mark), and shared all-gender rooms follow WAC 51-50-2902, subsection 2902.2.2. Unlike Tacoma's and Seattle's ordinances, the building code applies to new work and alterations, not to existing restrooms.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Spokane job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for the room and see the Spokane rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Spokane schools, hospitals and clinics, university buildings and restaurants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Washington's building rules, which Spokane enforces, require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Washington sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and Spokane applies the state count without changes. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Spokane requires a building permit to alter or repair a building unless the work is on the exempt list in the state building rules. The list covers "similar finish work" and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high, without naming toilet partitions, so ask the Spokane Development Services Center (509-625-6300) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** under Washington's building rules, which Spokane enforces, a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet and urinal is in its own compartment with full-height walls and a door that locks from the inside.
page.stalls_intro: Spokane uses Washington's count, which goes by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Washington sets its own count for schools, with more toilets for girls than for boys. Urinals are optional and may stand in for most of the men's toilets.
page.stalls_after: Small businesses may be allowed one shared restroom: up to 25 people in an office and up to 30 in a restaurant. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. Confirm your project with the Spokane Development Services Center.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor and a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet. A school is counted at one student per 100 square feet of the whole building. Your architect or the Spokane Development Services Center sets the final number.
extra_rule_bullets: - **Rule update planned for May 3, 2027:** Washington's code council plans to bring in the next edition of the state building and plumbing rules on that date. Spokane's code adopts whichever edition the state has in force, so the update applies in Spokane the same day.
page.install_rule: Washington requires every construction contractor to register with the Department of Labor & Industries (L&I). To take out a Spokane building permit, a contractor also needs a City of Spokane business license. Look a contractor up on the L&I website before you hire. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who takes out a Spokane permit needs a Washington L&I registration and a City of Spokane business license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Washington requires the state-set wage on every public job, with no minimum project size. The Department of Labor & Industries publishes the current Spokane County carpenter rate in its online wage lookup. Where federal money is in the project, the federal rate for a carpenter on building work in Spokane County is $44.21 an hour plus $17.28 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 9.1% in Spokane: 6.5% state and 2.6% local. On January 1, 2027 it rises to 9.3%, when the city and the county each add 0.1%.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals, medical offices and university buildings:** phenolic or stainless steel where restrooms are cleaned often, with accessible stalls in every room.
